extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of philosophy (advanced undergraduates, graduate students, and educated readers interested in philosophical method and ethics of belief)
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition of what Philosophy is (knowledge of the highest generality) and of its proper methodological/data requirements; also normative guidance for a 'catholic' thinker dealing with religious and doctrinal disagreement. Emphasizes provisional assumptions, verification by congruity with experience, and the social-ethical attitude toward other creeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patience and restraint in criticizing beliefs
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'catholic' thinker should display patience and restrain indignation when confronted with doctrines they regard as irrational or erroneous; they should avoid angry condemnation or ostentatious contempt even when repulsed by certain creeds' implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Though it may be hard in controversy, one must qualify antagonism in calmer moments so mature judgment and conduct remain unbiased. Avoid showing contempt publicly; temper immediate emotional reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize a fundamental verity within all religions
rubrics_metrics.description: In every form of religion there exists a 'soul of truth' — an essential verity that gives vitality to even degraded creeds and survives modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When condemning outward forms (dogmas, rites, traditions), remember the underlying truth they contain; do not throw away the protective 'envelopes' without considering the truth they preserve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess concrete religious elements by relative standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete elements of a creed that are bad by an absolute standard may nevertheless be good relative to the perceptions and needs of the people who hold them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat such elements as protective envelopes that make abstract verities appreciable; avoid abolishing forms that, for the present, are beneficial to the majority. Recognize need for continual readaptation as social characters change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim beyond mere toleration to recognize positive worth
rubrics_metrics.description: Toleration should be the widest possible, but the goal is not merely non-injustice; it is active justice through open recognition of the positive worth of alien beliefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualify disagreement with as much sympathy as possible; practice an active appreciation of whatever merit exists in opposing creeds rather than passive non-interference alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance conservative and progressive thought
rubrics_metrics.description: Both conservative (preserving existing institutions) and progressive (reforming/remodeling) thought and action must have free play because social progress requires continual readaptation effected by both forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not hesitate to express convictions even if ahead of the time; individuals are agents of social change and may properly voice inner beliefs, leaving their effects to unfold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophy as knowledge of the highest generality (complete unification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophy is knowledge of the highest degree of generality: whereas ordinary knowledge is ununified and science is partially unified, Philosophy is completely unified knowledge that integrates the widest generalizations of the sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish Philosophy (integration and synthesis of scientific generalizations into ultimate corollaries) from merely scientific or specialized inquiry. Philosophy's truths should consolidate and comprehend the broadest scientific generalizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of extracting common abstract truth from divergent conceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: To define Philosophy or any disputed concept, compare opinions of the same genus, set aside discordant concrete elements, and identify the remaining common abstract constituent that holds across modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comparative elimination of particular, erroneous, or excessive elements to render the tacit common element into a precise abstract expression; this is the method for finding philosophical definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not treat thoughts/data as isolable units
rubrics_metrics.description: Every thought involves a whole system of thoughts and cannot be meaningfully isolated from its correlatives; assuming a single datum in isolation conceals tacit, inseparable assumptions and produces circular reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of constructing arguments that purport to start from a single 'simple' datum; analyze implicit complementary thoughts (e.g., quantity, limit, difference, likeness) that are unavoidably involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisionally accept fundamental intuitions necessary for thought
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain fundamental intuitions or conceptions are vital to the very process of thinking and cannot be severed without mental dissolution; these must be assumed provisionally as true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat such assumptions as temporarily unquestionable and proceed to justify them by testing their consequences against experience; do not attempt to discard the basic conceptual framework that makes reasoning possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify philosophical assumptions by congruity with experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Assumptions are to be justified by demonstrating that the conclusions they yield correspond with directly observed facts — i.e., by showing congruity between ideal representations and actual experiences throughout the range of consciousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use successive tests and anticipated effects (analogous to scientific verification: weight, reaction to acid, malleability, etc.) to confirm hypotheses. The validity of a belief consists in its entire congruity with all other dicta of consciousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophy's task is proving congruity to achieve unification
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophy's business is to prove or disprove the congruity of its fundamental assumptions with all dicta of consciousness; complete establishment of congruity equals the complete unification of knowledge — Philosophy's goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The project is normative and cumulative: show agreement between all ideal and real states across experience; any discovered incongruity falsifies propositions in the usual sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize consciousness as the primary datum: likeness and unlikeness are cognizable
rubrics_metrics.description: A primordial datum for Philosophy is acceptance that congruities and incongruities (likenesses and unlikenesses) exist and are cognizable by consciousness; without this, no testing or establishment of congruity is possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept as basic the competence of consciousness to judge similarity and difference among its states, since such judgments are necessary both to falsify hypotheses and to achieve the philosophical ideal of perfect agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid claiming ultimate knowledge beyond the relative
rubrics_metrics.description: Given human intelligence's limitation to the relative, Philosophy must confine itself to unifying relative knowledge (the domain of Science) rather than attempting to reach 'absolute' or transcendent knowledge of ultimate Being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject ontological claims that purport to transcend consciousness's capacities; instead, integrate scientific generalizations and consider universal truths only insofar as they can be shown congruous with human experience.
